inspection.method: Opened actual original PNG with view_image before any candidate spec, draft or source SVG.

observations.pixels: One vertical F axis with upward arrow, one horizontal r axis with rightward arrow, origin marked 0. No numerical graduations, units, grid, table, or separate panels.
Solid upper force curve starts steeply near the upper center, descends to the right and flattens just above the horizontal axis. Chinese callout points to that upper curve.
Solid lower force curve starts low near the center, rises to the right and flattens below the horizontal axis. Chinese callout points to that lower curve.

Solid middle curve descends steeply from above zero, crosses the horizontal axis at the location labelled r0, continues to a rounded negative minimum, then rises toward the axis while staying between repulsion and attraction. Chinese interaction-force callout points to its upper branch.

The middle curve has a visibly thicker short section around its zero crossing, extending to both sides of r0. The crossing and label share the same horizontal position; the label is just above-left of the crossing.

Two dashed guide branches start on the F axis, one above and one below zero, and meet at a left junction on the r axis. To the right of that junction, a dashed upper and lower lobe surround the axis, attain opposite extrema close to the r0 horizontal position, and meet again on the r axis farther right. These guides are visibly dashed, unlike all three force curves.

interpretationBoundary: Pixel coordinates are approximate locators, not physical distances or force values. The dashed guides are recorded as visible guide geometry only; no extra physical meaning is assigned.
modernAdditions: English callouts replace source Chinese labels.
Canvas spacing, smooth curve regularization and unlabelled construction landmarks support readable deterministic rendering.
Semantic color roles distinguish net force, components and guides without replacing source solid/dashed/thickness distinctions.
